title: Nanoscale Investigation of Magnetic and Optical Properties of Strain-Engineered 2D Antiferromagnetic (VNi)PS3
content: Recent studies on 2D magnetic chalcophosphates (TMPQ3 TM = Mn, V, Fe, Co, Ni, Q = S, Se) have uncovered several exciting phenomena, including phonon-magnon coupling, charge-spin correlation, spin-correlated photon emissions [1-3]. These results position TMPQ3s as promising candidates for new spin-based devices, including 2D antiferromagnetic spintronics, optospintronics, magnonics, and spin caloritronics, among others [4-6]. Strain is a key lever for controlling magnetic and optical properties behavior in spin devices [5, 7]. Prior studies have demonstrated strain-induced effects such as chiral single photon emission, magnetic vector manipulation, and AFM-FM flipping with applied strain [8-10]. However, no investigations of the local strain state or structure have been completed to correlate to these resultant properties. Furthermore, defects such as stacking faults and rotational twins—common in mechanically exfoliated flakes—can cause strain, which can also affect local magnetic and optical properties, necessitating a closer examination of strain at the nanoscale.
